Siyan Yu

Master’s candidate in Civil and Hydraulic Engineering

I study how supply jets carry cool air into occupied spaces. I combine airflow visualization, temperature and velocity measurements, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to investigate ventilation in rooms and livestock buildings.

Email me
Master’s thesis · Rongchang, Chongqing

Targeted air supply and radiant cooling for boar houses

How effectively can a radiant panel cool a boar when fresh air is delivered directly to its pen? In the July–September 2026 field campaign, I helped lead the design and construction of the test platform and planned the measurements. I recorded pen airspeeds, air and panel temperatures, humidity, and animal responses to evaluate cooling performance and check the CFD predictions against field measurements.

Experimental research

November 2025 – January 2026

Airflow in a scaled pig farm

I helped build the scaled experimental platform and measured airflow and temperature distributions. We compared five turbulence models against the measurements and selected the realizable k–ε model for subsequent simulations.

June – November 2025

Stratum ventilation under cooling conditions

I measured air velocity and temperature at multiple locations with a SWEMA 03+ omnidirectional anemometer. Smoke visualization helped us trace the downward path of the cool jet in the occupied zone as we investigated supply temperature, velocity, and discharge angle.

August – October 2025

Deflected cooling jets

I fabricated deflection dampers, helped assemble the test rig, and used smoke and laser illumination to visualize jets from grille diffusers. Our measurements informed a model of how centreline velocity decays along the wall.
